objective: Quantify how seller-state -> customer-state transportation performance (delivery delay, freight cost, distance) evolves by purchase month for the four target product categories, and forecast the per-state-pair monthly average delivery delay 12 months ahead with ARIMA(1,1,1); persist a historical summary, forecasts and state-pair aggregates to SQLite plus overall KPIs to JSON.
analysis_type: descriptive spatiotemporal aggregation (3-way grain) + per-series univariate time-series forecasting + distributional summary

inputs.role: fact table: order_id, order_item_id, product_id, seller_id, freight_value

inputs.notes: 610 null categories; no products with null category will survive the category filter
header carries a UTF-8 BOM -> must read with encoding='utf-8-sig' and strip BOM from the first column name

inputs.role: order header: order_status, order_purchase_timestamp (month), order_delivered_customer_date, order_estimated_delivery_date
inputs.notes: order_status delivered = 96478; 2965 null delivered dates, 0 null estimated dates
customer_id is order-scoped (1 row per order), so it acts as the order->customer bridge
551 duplicated order_id values -> keep latest review per order by review_answer_timestamp

inputs.role: zip_code_prefix -> raw geocoded points; must be collapsed to one centroid (mean lat, mean lng) per prefix
inputs.notes: 19015 distinct zip prefixes; up to hundreds of rows per prefix; zip prefixes are 5-char zero-padded strings

inputs.role: upstream profiling artifact: schema, dtypes, nulls, key_facts used as expected-value reference
upstream artifacts already present in workspace; used only as a cross-check baseline for shapes and KPI magnitudes, never rewritten by inference

environment.implication: The pipeline must be written in pure standard-library Python: csv.DictReader for IO, dict-based hash joins/grouping, statistics.mean for averages, math for haversine, sqlite3 for persistence. ARIMA(1,1,1) cannot be imported and must be implemented explicitly (CSS/LS estimation of phi, theta, constant by grid + local refinement), with the historical-mean/std fallback kept as hard requirement.

data_quality_findings.issue: geolocation has many rows per zip prefix
data_quality_findings.impact: join without aggregation multiplies order rows
data_quality_findings.handling: pre-aggregate to 19015 prefix centroids before joining; never join raw geolocation to facts
dedupe: latest by review_answer_timestamp, tie-break review_id
require order_status == 'delivered' AND non-null delivered & estimated dates

data_quality_findings.issue: orders whose status is delivered but with null delivered date

data_quality_findings.handling: keep NaN, do not impute; count affected monthly groups

data_quality_findings.impact: single-order groups produce noisy/noisy monthly series
data_quality_findings.handling: keep them (grain is data-driven) but require >=6 monthly points per state pair for ARIMA; reference month span 2016-10..2018-08 = 21 months

data_quality_findings.impact: an order can belong to several seller states
data_quality_findings.handling: grain is (seller_state, customer_state, month); an order row is counted once per pair, order-level metrics de-duplicated by order_id, item-level metrics (freight, distance) on the item grain

join_chain: order_items order_id,customer_id -> orders (order_status=='delivered', delivered & estimated dates non-null)
order_items product_id -> products (product_category_name) -> translation (english) -> keep ONLY {telephony, computers_accessories, electronics, consoles_games}
customer/seller zip prefixes -> geolocation centroids (mean lat/lng per prefix)

stages.name: load geolocation centroids
stages.action: single streaming pass over olist_geolocation_dataset.csv accumulating sum(lat), sum(lng), count per zip prefix -> centroid dict; load to SQLite temp table optional

stages.name: category filter set
stages.action: translation (utf-8-sig) -> Portuguese category names for the 4 target English names (telefonia, informatica_acessorios, eletronicos, consoles_games); build set of matching product_ids from products.csv

stages.name: fact build / join
stages.action: stream order_items, keep rows whose product_id is in filtered set; join orders/customers/sellers/reviews/centroids; parse timestamps with datetime.strptime (format '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'); purchase_month = '%Y-%m'; delivery_delay_days = (delivered_customer_date.date() - estimated_delivery_date.date()).days; haversine per item
stages.output: item-level records with keys (seller_state, customer_state, purchase_month) and order-level de-dup view

stages.name: group aggregation
stages.action: aggregate per (seller_state, customer_state, purchase_month): avg delivery delay and avg review on de-duplicated order grain; total_orders = distinct order_id count; avg freight and avg haversine on item grain

stages.name: state-pair aggregates
stages.action: re-aggregate the same records (or the summary) to (seller_state, customer_state) keeping columns avg_delivery_delay_days, avg_review_score, total_orders, avg_haversine_distance_km (freight dropped per spec)

stages.name: monthly series extraction
stages.action: per (seller_state, customer_state) collect the month->avg_delivery_delay_days series sorted chronologically; select pairs with >= 6 monthly points

stages.name: ARIMA(1,1,1) per qualifying pair
stages.action: fit ARIMA(1,1,1) on the delay series (d=1 differencing, AR(1)+MA(1)+constant), forecast 12 steps; forecast_mean = mean of 12 forecast values, forecast_std = population std of the 12 forecast values; on any fit failure (non-finite, non-convergence, <6 points, degenerate variance) fall back to historical mean and population std of the series and flag it

stages.name: persist artifacts
stages.action: drop+recreate the three SQLite tables with explicit column order/dtypes (TEXT/REAL/INTEGER), bulk insert with executemany, sort as specified before insert; write output.json with the 6 overall KPIs rounded to 4 decimals

stages.name: validation
stages.action: run the checks listed in validation_checks; abort-with-report if any hard check fails

metric_definitions.delivery_delay_days: (order_delivered_customer_date - order_estimated_delivery_date) in whole days; negative = delivered before the estimate; order-level metric
metric_definitions.avg_delivery_delay_days: mean delivery_delay_days over the distinct orders of the group
metric_definitions.avg_review_score: mean review_score over the distinct orders of the group that have a (deduped) review
metric_definitions.total_orders: count of distinct order_id in the group (not item rows)
metric_definitions.avg_freight_value: mean freight_value over order-item rows in the group (spec: not multiplied by quantity)
metric_definitions.avg_haversine_distance_km: mean over order-item rows of haversine(R=6371 km) between seller zip centroid and customer zip centroid; NaN when either prefix lacks a centroid
metric_definitions.avg_delivery_delay_overall: mean of delivery_delay_days over all in-scope distinct orders (order-level, not a mean of group means)
metric_definitions.avg_review_score_overall: mean review_score over all in-scope orders with a review
metric_definitions.avg_haversine_distance_overall: mean haversine over all in-scope order items with both centroids
metric_definitions.total_state_pairs: count of distinct (seller_state, customer_state) pairs in the historical summary
metric_definitions.total_months: count of distinct purchase_month values in the historical summary

sqlite_contract.notes: NaN/None must be stored as SQL NULL; no unnamed index column; no extra tables other than the three specified

validation_checks.check: row counts: spatiotemporal_summary ~1844, state_pair_stats = number of distinct pairs in summary (243), arima_forecast = pairs with >=6 months (121)
no duplicate (seller_state, customer_state, purchase_month) in spatiotemporal_summary; no duplicate pair in arima_forecast / state_pair_stats

total_orders in summary sums to the overall distinct order count (14143) only if orders map to a single pair; otherwise >= that count -> verify sum(items-per-pair) consistency instead of naive equality
all four target categories represented; spot-check that a telephony-only order is included and a 'health_beauty' order is excluded

purchase_month values match ^
\d{4}-\d{2}$ and lie within 2016-10..2018-08
haversine distances positive and mostly < 4000 km (Brazil extent); no negative or absurd values
avg_review_score within [1,5] where not null; avg_delivery_delay_days within a plausible [-120, 200] band; report count of NULLs in avg_review_score (ref 4) and avg_haversine (ref 9)
forecast_mean finite; forecast_std >= 0; count of ARIMA fallbacks reported (reference baseline: 0 fallbacks)
tables sorted exactly per spec when read back without ORDER BY; column names/order/types match contract
output.json contains exactly the 6 required keys with correct types
reconciliation: overall delay/review computed from raw order-level facts equals the KPI in output.json (weighted, not mean-of-means)

cross-check magnitudes against upstream baseline (output.json: 243 pairs, 21 months, -11.77 days, 4.08 score, 14143 orders, 677.31 km) - same order of magnitude expected, differences must be explainable

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: stdlib-only implementation; hand-rolled ARIMA(1,1,1) (CSS with grid search over phi/theta then coordinate refinement), fallback to historical mean/std on failure

risks_and_mitigations.risk: geolocation join fan-out blows up memory/time
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: aggregate to 19015 centroids in one streaming pass first; stream facts and never materialise raw geolocation twice

risks_and_mitigations.risk: ARIMA on 6-7 point series can diverge or produce extreme forecasts
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: bounded parameter search, finite-value guards, clip explosive forecasts, and the mandated mean/std fallback

risks_and_mitigations.risk: order counted in multiple seller_state pairs
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: de-duplicate order-level metrics within each group; document that total_orders per group is pair-scoped

risks_and_mitigations.risk: type drift in SQLite (ints stored as float, NaN stored as string)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: explicit schema DDL, int() casts for total_orders, None for NaN, read-back type assertions

risks_and_mitigations.risk: hard-coded order of rows not guaranteed by SQLite
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: insert in final sorted order and verify read-back order in V9

downstream_handoff.implementation_notes: Execute stages S1..S9 in order; S1-S3 can be one script that caches an intermediate JSONL of in-scope records (order grain + item grain) so S4-S8 rerun cheaply within the 120 s tool limit.
